<h1 align="center">CASTAWAY</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>Ten hours on a very small island. She idles. The plumbing is just for the README.</b><br>
  <sub>working title &middot; an unofficial remake, inspired by the 1992 desert-island screensaver <i>Johnny Castaway</i> &middot; in development</sub>
</p>

Castaway is a stationary-frame lo-fi video for YouTube, in the spirit of the ten-hour lofi streams: a young woman alone on a tiny island with one tall palm, a raft and a lot of time. She mostly idles, nodding to the music on her headphones, and every so often something happens. A message in a bottle washes straight back. A delivery drone drops a parcel, and the parcel is another pair of headphones. A coconut falls on a hermit crab, and then the coconut walks off. It is sunny, hand-painted coastal anime, 16:9 at 1080p, and it is always daytime, by rule.

More than 90 activities live in [activities.toml](activities.toml), on four timers: everyday routines every 2 to 5 minutes, up to super-rare callbacks every 3 to 6 hours. They run on six **lanes**, so things can overlap, and that is what the pipes above are: her, the sea and sky, the turtle, the cat, the shore and the kumara patch, one pipe each, passing in front of and behind one another. Everything starts on the next bar of the music, every 3 seconds, so the gags land on the beat (so do the pipes). Every sound is synthesized from code by [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no loops, no recordings.

```sh
python tools/serve.py
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

<p align="center">
  <sub>Live preview in the browser, then export a YouTube-ready MP4: the page encodes the frames, the server mixes in the sound.<br>
  Plain ES modules, no build step, no npm. Nothing is published yet, so for now the only way to watch her do nothing is to run it.</sub>
</p>

<details>
<summary><b>SCREEN SAVER SETTINGS</b>: what the pipes mean, and how the banner is built</summary>

```text
┌─ Screen Saver Settings ────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                                            │
│  Saver ............. Castaway Plumbing, by Tidewater Tubeworks             │
│  Pipes ............. 6, one per lane of the schedule:                      │
│                      her · sea+sky · turtle · cat · shore · kumara         │
│  Speed ............. one segment per sixteenth note, at 80 BPM             │
│  New pipes ......... on the next bar line only (one bar = 3 s)             │
│  Her pipe .......... busy 1 bar in 3, idle the rest. like her              │
│  Joint type ........ ( ) Ball   ( ) Elbow   (•) Mixed, 1 ball in 3         │
│  Surface ........... (•) Glossy   ( ) Brushed   ( ) Woodgrain              │
│  Rare fitting ...... [x] Coconut     odds: 1 per loop (rounded up)         │
│  Clear screen ...... after bar 19, by dissolve, 16 waves in one bar        │
│  Loop .............. 20 bars, 60 s: exactly one turn of the theme          │
│  Camera ............ perspective, 8 layers deep, never moves               │
│  Password .......... [ ] off. she could leave any time                     │
│                                                                            │
│                    [ Preview ]     [   OK   ]     [ Cancel ]               │
│                                                                            │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**The idea.** The island has no plumbing. The schedule, it turns out, does. Each lane in [activities.toml](activities.toml) is a track that one thing can be busy on at a time: her, the cat, the turtle, the sea and sky, the shore, the kumara patch. Two lanes can be busy at once, which is how a ship gets past while she is up to her elbows in a coconut. In the banner every lane is a pipe colour, and the pipes keep to the same rules as the video: a new one may only start on a bar line, and her pipe is busy one bar in three and idle the rest, because she is.

**The loop.** Sixteenth notes at 80 BPM are 0.1875 s, which is about the speed the old screensaver grew at, so every pipe gains one segment per sixteenth. Twenty bars of 3 s make 60 s, the length of the theme, so the banner loops when the music would. Nineteen bars of growing, one bar of dissolving, and round again. The banner opens six bars in, so nobody has to watch an empty screen first.

**The plumbing.** A generator walks six lanes through a grid of cells eight layers deep, seen through a real perspective camera, so near pipes are fat and far ones thin. Each straight run is one SVG path whose round cross-section is shaded by a gradient worked out from a light, a diffuse term and a white specular highlight; each joint is a sphere shaded the same way. Which piece is drawn over which is decided properly: any two pieces sit in different grid cells, so a flat plane separates them, and the side of the plane with the eye on it wins. That gives a list of "this goes over that" for every overlap, which is sorted in one pass. Growth is a stepped stroke dash, one segment at a time, with no smooth sliding: hard cuts and stepped movement are the house style of the video too. No script, no fonts, no filters, about 140 KB. With reduced motion switched on it holds still on the picture as it stands after bar 13.

**The name** is built from the same ivory plumbing, ball fittings at every tee and open end, and she sits on the second A nodding at 80 BPM: 80 nods a loop, and not one missed. In the original screensaver the rare joint was a teapot. Here it is a coconut, and it turns up once every loop, because a 1 in 1,000 coconut is a coconut nobody sees.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>THE LANES</b>: what actually runs down each pipe, and how often</summary>

```text
 LANE      WHAT RUNS DOWN IT
 ────────  ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 HER       coconut sipping, fishing, jogging laps, a sandcastle, waving
           for rescue. a message in a bottle (it washes straight back;
           much later a different bottle brings a reply). a coconut that
           falls on a hermit crab, then walks off with the crab wearing
           it. the signal hunt: one bar of signal, at the top of the palm.
           bushcraft: fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm,
           spear fishing. planting a kumara. and, very rarely, walking
           out over the water and coming back with an iced coffee
 SEA+SKY   the ship, which sails past while she is busy. shared with her:
           a delivery drone (the parcel is more headphones), a tour boat
           of selfie-takers, a shark in headphones nodding to the beat,
           a bro on an electric hydrofoil (a shaka, a carve, gone)
 TURTLE    a sea turtle, who visits
 CAT       a grey tabby with a white chest. arrives on a crate, climbs
           the palm, naps, and one day floats away again. comes back
           another time
 SHORE     the tide, which takes the sandcastle and the delivery box
 KUMARA    the kumara she planted, growing over the course of the video
 ────────  ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

 TIMER        COMES ROUND EVERY       IN A TYPICAL 10-HOUR RUN
 regular      2 to 5 minutes          about 155
 occasional   12 to 25 minutes        about 30
 rare         30 to 60 minutes        about 13
 super rare   3 to 6 hours            about 2 (never more than 3)
 chained      when another one says   follow-ups: the tide, the reply
 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 counts: the median of 200 simulated runs. she is busy about a third of
 the time and idling the rest. every start waits for the next bar.
 default run: 10:00:00, seed 1992. always daytime
```

Run `python tools/schedule.py` to check the schedule and simulate a ten-hour run, lane by lane. Around the island, 26 bits of scene life keep the frame breathing: shore waves and drifting cloud shadows are built, and distant birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are planned.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>THE TOOLS, THE SOUND</b>, the credits and the greetz</summary>

```text
 TOOL                                  WHAT IT DOES
 ────────────────────────────────────  ─────────────────────────────────
 python tools/serve.py                 the renderer: a web page with a
                                       live preview, at
                                       http://127.0.0.1:8765/
 export (in the page)                  frame-exact H.264 in the browser
                                       (WebCodecs); the server mixes the
                                       sound and joins the two into an
                                       MP4 for YouTube
 python tools/schedule.py              validates the schedule, simulates
                                       a ten-hour run
 python tools/render_demo.py --dev     a dev reel of every activity with
                                       a heads-up display (the older
                                       Python reference renderer)
 python tools/make_audio.py            synthesizes every sound, from code
 ────────────────────────────────────  ─────────────────────────────────

 THE SOUND
   theme ......... a seamless 60 s loop, 80 BPM, F major, ii-V-I-vi,
                   20 bars of exactly 3 s: electric piano, a kalimba
                   lead, soft drums, vinyl crackle
   ocean ......... also a seamless 60 s loop
   everything .... more than 150 sound files, all made from code. no
                   samples, loops or recordings, so no third-party
                   licence applies
   levels ........ -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBTP; a master
                   level and one per routine
   heard by ...... nobody yet. so far only the loudness meter has an
                   opinion, and it is keeping it to itself
```

Working notes, decisions and the things still open live in [MUSING.md](MUSING.md). The page itself is [web/index.html](web/index.html).

**Credits.** The island, her and every gag: Castaway. The inspiration: *Johnny Castaway* (1992), which belongs to its owners; this is an unofficial remake, in spirit only, and he does not appear. The banner's style: the glossy 3D pipes screensaver from the mid-90s OpenGL era, redrawn from scratch here with nothing copied but the idea of pipes; its rare teapot joint is honoured with a coconut. The banner: Castaway Plumbing, by Tidewater Tubeworks, who do not exist and have never fitted a pipe.

**Greetz** to the Elbow Room Waiting Society (members wait between bars, on purpose), the Plumbers' Guild of Islands With No Plumbing (one member, very relaxed), and the Standpipe Lunchtime Choir (eighty nods a minute, eyes closed, never out of time).

</details>

<p align="center"><sub>Tidewater Tubeworks, Castaway Plumbing, the Elbow Room Waiting Society, the Plumbers' Guild of Islands With No Plumbing and the Standpipe Lunchtime Choir are invented. The pipes are not connected to anything, which is also true of the island.</sub></p>
